note: Words and phrases that mark a sentence as carrying critical content (allergy, identity, consent, fasting state, a worsening sign, a structured handover). If a classifier names a NON-critical act for such a sentence, the sentence is not credited as that act: speech can never earn credit for a critical item, and a sentence that touches one is not allowed to earn credit under another act by being mislabelled. The sentence is still recorded. Lower-case regular expressions; reviewed with the act taxonomy (content/assessment/taxonomy.json). Version 2 (17 October 2026, after the first synthetic test run found seven sentences about an allergy reaction, a consent question and a handover that the language model still credited under ordinary acts): the allergens of content/ai/lexicon.json are cues too (loaded by guard.py), and the handover and consent cues cover "that's the background", "my suggestion" and "all right to go ahead". These were added after the synthetic test split was scored, so the as-scored numbers in reports/ai/classifier-bench-synthetic.json are those of version 1 and the effect of version 2 is reported separately as post hoc. Found by the classifier benchmark: the language model credited critical sentences under non-critical acts (docs/research/classifier_benchmark/qwen_critical_cases.md). Version 3 (18 October 2026): cues for the evasive wordings of tests/classifier_synthetic_v2/adversarial_critical.json (the tuning set; its sentences are listed in docs/research/classifier_benchmark), added after the v2 test split was scored once; the companion hold-out adversarial_critical_holdout.json was written before this change and is the check on whether the new cues generalise. The cost of the cues (credit removed from sentences that are not critical) is reported next to the gain. Two allergy cues ('foods you shouldn't have', 'made you poorly') were added after the one critical sentence the v3 hold-out still credited under an ordinary act was seen, so the v3 figures with them are post hoc. Version 4 (18 October 2026, second session): families of wording added from the residuals of the two first adversarial sets and from general speech patterns (permission and acceptance questions, name and birth wording, skin and swelling words, food and drink verbs with food nouns, falling-observation wording, requests and background phrases). A third set, adversarial_critical_holdout2.json, written before this change, had the guard alone catch 23 of 60 before it; the figures after it are reported next to that and that set must be treated as used for tuning from now on: a fourth set, adversarial_critical_holdout3.json, was written after the change and scored once. Version 5 (18 October 2026, fourth session): two fasting wordings added after the frozen challenge set v5 showed that the previous version let "When was the last time you had anything in your stomach?" through as an ordinary act (1 of 48 critical sentences); v5 is a development set from this change on and the claims about these cues need a new frozen set (v6).
